paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the leaders asked Jesus a question they didn't really want answered. They asked, "By what authority are You doing these things?" (Mark 11:28), but when He asked about John's baptism, they started working out which answer would cost them the least. If they said, "From heaven," they figured He would ask, "Why then did you not believe him?" (Mark 11:31), and if they said, "From men," they were afraid of the people (Mark 11:32). So they said, "We do not know." (Mark 11:33), and I think they knew a lot more than they let on.

Then Jesus tells about a man who planted a vineyard and rented it to tenants, and the tenants beat and killed the servants he sent. Last, he sent "one beloved son" (Mark 12:6), and they killed him too. Jesus asks, "What then will the owner of the vineyard do?" and answers that he will come, kill those tenants and give the vineyard to others (Mark 12:9). That's the warning, friend: rejecting the owner's son doesn't end with the tenants keeping the vineyard, and verse 12 says the leaders knew He had spoken this parable against them.

So what does that mean for you, baker? Jesus is the stone the builders rejected, and Scripture says it "has become the cornerstone. This is from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes" (Mark 12:10-11). People can push Him out, and He still ends up in the most important spot. Don't ask about Him just to protect your own place. Ask because you want the answer, and then let Him have the spot that is already His.
